A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HypeVPR and are readable throughout, including their equations, figures and tables. Neither contains an appendix or embedded supplement; both reference separate supplementary material that is unavailable in the supplied PDFs.

before.justification: v2 reports original retrieval experiments on Pitts250K-P2E and YQ360, efficiency comparisons, and feature-space and loss ablations in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v3 reports original retrieval results and ablations in Tables 1–5, including an added SF-XL evaluation and an empirical descriptor visualization.

M1.justification: v3 replaces exponential-distance reranking scores with candidate-wise Z-score normalization before weighted fusion (v2 Eqs. 16–17; v3 Eqs. 18–20). The hierarchy, hyperbolic averaging and three training losses remain. v3 also explicitly describes GeM followed by linear projections, although the PDFs do not establish whether those projections were previously implemented but undocumented.

E1.justification: Pitts250K-P2E and YQ360 remain. SF-XL, previously mentioned as pretraining provenance, becomes an evaluation domain: v3 tests against 0.23M panoramas representing 2.8M perspective database images. This substantially extends geographic and large-database evaluation coverage beyond the earlier experiments.

E2.justification: The external comparator sets in the retained Pitts250K-P2E and YQ360 comparisons remain unchanged. New SF-XL Table 3 evaluates CricaVPR, BoQ and SALAD-slim, which had no reported comparison rows in v2, alongside retained methods such as EigenPlace, CosPlace and SALAD.

E3.justification: v3 reports 512-pixel P2P queries instead of v2's universal 224-pixel setup and replaces fixed 0.2/0.8 fusion weights with validation-selected weights. The loss ablation changes from an eight-window Swin-Tiny configuration to HypeVPR-O under Table 2 settings. Added protocols include SF-XL query v1 with a converted panoramic database and ResNet-50 P2E configurations.

E4.justification: v3 adds a lowest-level-only HypeVPR-SW control to test hierarchical score fusion and visualizes 1,000 hierarchical descriptors in Figure 4. The loss-removal study is revised under a different configuration. The two-level Euclidean-versus-hyperbolic comparison and qualitative retrieval examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither supplied PDF reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v3's Z-score normalization is part of retrieval scoring, not statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds SF-XL results, ResNet-50 P2E rows and the HypeVPR-SW result. On SF-XL, HypeVPR-L reports R@1 85.2, versus SALAD's 88.6, with lower matching time and storage. Retained entries also change: Table 1's Swin-Tiny eight-window Pitts recalls become 29.4/51.4/60.6 instead of 26.6/48.6/58.8. Table 2 recalls are updated, several narrative speedup ratios are corrected, and the loss-ablation results are replaced under different settings; these are not uniformly same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v3 Section 3.1 adds explicit definitions of the Poincare-ball domain, Riemannian metric and conformal factor, which v2 did not provide, together with a geodesic-distance expression. These are limited formal additions; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion narrow the headline accuracy claim from outperforming existing methods or achieving state-of-the-art performance to competitive or comparable accuracy with favorable efficiency. The central contributions—hyperbolic hierarchical aggregation and adjustable retrieval—remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds an explicit limitation concerning compatibility with standard kNN tools such as FAISS. It interprets the new descriptor visualization as evidence of semantic hierarchy and explains how overlapping windows disrupt triplet positive–negative relationships. The existing interpretations of complementary losses and hyperbolic aggregation largely remain.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies curvature c=1, an NVIDIA A5000 GPU, CPU matching and default hierarchy depth L=5. It omits v2's explicit shortlist sizes of 200/40, horizontal-flip augmentation and Pitts-to-YQ360 fine-tuning description, and does not give the selected fusion weights. The direct code link becomes a project-page pointer. Omitted descriptions do not establish that the corresponding procedures stopped.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations supporting hierarchical visual context, additional VPR developments, ConvNeXt and the FAISS limitation. The Matryoshka analogy and citation, and the TextPlace citation, disappear. The main positioning against sliding-window P2E methods and within hyperbolic representation learning remains.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, with substantial editing across the method, experimental discussion and conclusion. v3 introduces numbered sections, separates HAM into its own subsection, reorganizes implementation details and standardizes model names as HypeVPR-O/B/L/SW. This is a broad narrative revision beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: v3 moves Figure 1 to the opening page and adds a radar comparison, redraws Figure 2 with a HAM panel, drops the standalone panorama-splitting diagram, and adds a descriptor visualization. Table 1 gains backbone information, new grouping and highlighting; an SF-XL table is added. The qualitative retrieval figure is retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The SF-XL evaluation and sliding-window control strengthen support for scalability and hierarchical fusion. v3 also corrects several speedup ratios, improves method presentation, narrows headline accuracy claims and acknowledges a search-library limitation. These benefits outweigh the loss of some implementation detail, but omitted shortlist and weight values, together with the remaining sub-millisecond claim inconsistent with Table 1, limit the overall improvement.
